messages:
alex_support: @maya_eng @rachel_sre ACME reported p99 spike after cobalt-3 onboarding. They saw p99 jump ~320ms → ~1.2s on long-context requests. Attached curl and trimmed logs.

alex_support: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'X-Model: cobalt-3' -d '{"input":"<12k token payload>"}'

alex_support: log snippet:
```
request_id=tr-9f3a p95=220ms p99=1120ms step=tokenize cpu=93% kv_cache_hit=false
```

maya_eng: looking into traces — tokenizer time is 800-1000ms for these long inputs, not the serving step. :eyes:

jon_oncall: can we rollback tokenizer change for cobalt-3 in prod? Canary only on 2 nodes right now.

rachel_sre: initiating rollback/fallback policy — routing cobalt-3 -> cobalt-3-v1 for affected customers. rolling in 5m. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Canary rollback job started by @rachel_sre — job id rb-87421

maya_eng: repro locally with same payload (12k tokens) — confirmed p99 ~1.1s. hypothesis: new merge-order produces longer subtokens causing extra tokenization work + KV cache misses on long prefixes.

maya_eng: quick mitigation: set TOKENIZER_PROFILE=legacy-bpe or force model tag cobalt-3-v1. I'll open PR to pin merge order and add metric for produced_subtokens.

taylor_product: I'll notify ACME support contact and update the incident ticket with workaround (model=cobalt-3-v1). Creating follow-up JIRA for SLO test expansion.

jon_oncall: also add synthetic long-context tokenization test to the console SLO suite to catch regressions.

maya_eng: root cause narrow: merge-order change caused non-deterministic split sizes leading to cache alignment regression when sequence>8k. PR #4523 fixes stable-merge-order + adds produced_subtokens gauge. Patching to staging now.

rachel_sre: rollback completed. Routing confirmed. Customer confirmed latency back to baseline after switching to cobalt-3-v1. :tada:

alex_support: closing thread for now — keep watch for PR rollout metrics. Reopen if p99 doesn't come down.
